title: The little light
premise: A gust blows out Pip's lantern on the way to the lighthouse. The path ends at a gap, and Wick can't see to light the lamp.

scenes.summary: Pip's lantern blows out on the shore path

problem.summary: The lantern has rolled to the dark edge of the page

actions.text: Down where lost things wash ashore, a small fox kept a small light.
No, no, no...
It rolled right to the edge. And it's so dark over there.
Could you reach it for me?
It's lit! It was cold, and then you held it, and it just... woke up.
Thank you. I'm not scared now. Well. A bit less.
It's warmer than it's ever been. Like it remembers your hand.
It had never burned so brightly. It was, after all, the first light anyone had ever handed back to him.

actions.outcome: the Reader carried the lantern back, glowing

actions.text: Oh! That's kind of you.
But my lantern's still over there, in the dark.
Nobody came. So the little fox took a deep breath, and went to the edge all by himself.
And when he held it close, brave in the dark, the little flame woke up again.
I did it. I really did it!

actions.outcome: brave in the dark, he fetched it himself

actions.text: Wick will be lighting the lamp soon. I'm meant to help him.
Down where the house ends, everything lost drifts home in the end. Buttons. Spoons. Odd socks. And once, a whole umbrella.
Somebody's missing a very big button.
I hope they're not cold without it.
What was that? Who's there?
Only a moth. Moths are never lost. Only distracted.
Moth! You frightened me. And mind your feelers, it's hot!
No, Moth. It isn't for eating. It's for seeing.
See? Out there it's only sand. Dark sand. Nothing to be scared of.
Mostly nothing.
Wick says the lighthouse calls every lost thing home. Every night, round and round.
He says one day it might be my job.
I'd have to stop being scared of the dark first.
The dark didn't say anything. It never does. It only waited, the way it always had, for someone brave enough to walk into it.
Come on, Moth. It's this way. Stay close.

scenes.summary: The path ends at a gap, and the lighthouse is dark

problem.summary: The path ends at a gap, and the lighthouse is on the other side

actions.text: The path went on, and on, and then it simply stopped.
Oh. The lighthouse is right there. I can see the door.
Wick? Wick! He can't hear me from all the way over here.
Maybe if I take a run at it...
No. No, no. Much too far.
It's easy for you, Moth. You've got wings.
Lost things had been falling into that gap for years and years. Far below, the sea kept them.
If only we could cross... Is there anything in that drawer?
A kite? In this wind?
I'm flying! I'm really, actually flying!
Thread! If only someone could carry the end across...
The moth only wanted to be near the light. But it carried the thread across all the same.
A ladder! If I lay it down flat, it's a bridge!
Don't look down. Don't look down. Don't look down.
A sock? It's far too short to reach across.
But it is very warm. Thank you.
Something longer, maybe? Or something that flies?
A key. Maybe the gap is... locked?
Moth, it's not a light, it's a key!
I don't think gaps have keyholes. Is there something to get me over?
Hmm. I don't think this will get me across.
Is there something longer? Or something that flies?
What's all this shouting about? Who's there?
Wick! It's me! I can't get across!
Hmph. Hold still, lad. And catch.
Hand over paw, hand over paw...
You're shaking like a leaf, lad.
I'm fine. I'm fine. Is it always this dark out here?
Every night. That's rather the point of us.
And what do you think you're doing, crossing chasms in the dark?
Someone helped me. Someone very big.
Someone very big? Up there?
They opened the drawer. They just reached in and handed it to me.
Hmph. Well. Thank you kindly, whoever you are.
Come on then, lad. That lamp won't light itself.
They walked the last of the path together, the old badger and the small fox, toward the dark tower.
Forty years I've lit that lamp. Every single night.
Even when it stormed?
Especially when it stormed.
But tonight the lighthouse stood dark. On a night like this, it had never once been dark.
Can't see the wick to light it. Not like I used to.
Don't you go telling anyone.
I won't. But I've still got my light.
So up they went, a hundred and twelve steps, round and round, to the lamp at the very top.
And the little light became the big one, and swept out over every lost thing in the house.
Not bad, keeper.
Keeper?
Every keeper has a first night. Don't let it go to your head.
Look! It reaches all the way out to you.
Same time tomorrow, keeper?
Same time tomorrow.
Far out in the dark, something lost turned toward the light, and started for home.
And whatever the Reader gave that night, the book kept safe, for another time.
Because lost things, as you'll find, have a way of coming back.
Somewhere out past the edge of the table, the sea went on breathing.
The wind moved through the reeds, and the night waited.
